newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa up but off highs, NY fails to shine.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa up but off highs, NY fails to shine.

text.p: Cocoa prices gave up some early gains after New York failed to extend its overnight rally but prices still finished firmer on Friday but near their day's floor.
Traders said some selling emerged in the afternoon after what appeared to be lack of follow-through fund buying in New York.
"There's no apparent resumption of fund buying in New York, that's why we came down a bit this afternoon. I think the market was expecting to see it."
Traders said the weaker U.S. dollar after a heavy bout of profit-taking also helped support New York and put some pressure on London.
Benchmark May whizzed past the initial technical hurdle of 1,027 stg earlier in the session to hit a new seven-month-high of 1,032 per tonne.
But the contract pulled back to close at 1,020 stg, still a 14 stg gain. Traders said Thursday's strong close in New York had fuelled the early rally amid continued short covering and fresh buying.
"Switches tightened again which is an indication that levels might be higher still," said one trader.
Volume was brisk at 16,228 lots, dominated by switches and AA trades. Dec 1997 and March 1998 were very active on price fixations against physical contracts.
Some traders said the market has probably seen its tentative top and could consolidate at these high levels.
But there was no change in the supply scenario while the views of some analysts that the season will end with a sizeable production deficit was already discounted in the market, traders said.
Some traders said the rally in New York could have been fuelled by funds shifting money out of coffee, which took a sharp downturn on Thursday, and into cocoa.
